primitives.name: Joint Production Division
primitives.verbatim_quote: JOINT PRODUCTION AND CAPITALIZATION 95 two serious new problems, though closely related; first, the mechanism of the actual organization of productive groups through free contract alone, and, second, the division of a joint product among the individuals making different kinds of contributions to its production.
primitives.assumptions: Free contract, given resources, fixed methods of production, individual contributions are measurable.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs when individual contributions cannot be separated or valued independently.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) framework for extreme event redistribution, treating joint products as correlated assets.
layer2.telemetry: Market liquidity and asset price co-movement serve as empirical verification metrics.

The eight source passages introduce foundational issues in resource allocation and value distribution within economic systems. Joint production creates a dual challenge: coordinating productive groups through voluntary contracts and fairly dividing outputs among contributors. This leads to the classic 'problem of imputation,' which seeks to assign value to each input factor based on its marginal contribution. The transition from theoretical specialized production to practical joint production reveals the complexity of real-world social organization under free exchange. The primitives formalize these concepts into rigorous mathematical structures: joint production division addresses the computational problem of apportioning shared outputs, while the problem of imputation provides tools for tracing value back to inputs. Social organization under free exchange and joint production practice offer axiomatic frameworks for market coordination and collective action respectively. These operators are interconnected through duality principles—division and imputation are mathematically inverse operations—and they collectively form a structural lens for analyzing economic systems. Failure modes include non-convex production sets, indivisibilities, and strategic behavior that disrupts efficient allocations. The derived kernels map these abstract primitives to concrete applications in Galaxy Sports Intelligence (GSI) and Galaxy Sports Engine (GSE), enabling probabilistic forecasting and situational reasoning in dynamic environments.
